title: Forest-floor plants in French (2005-2022) and Swedish (1994-2024) inventories shifted to warmer niches at 32-46% of full climate tracking; local warming rate explained the pattern only in Sweden
abstract: Question: did forest-floor plant communities shift toward warm-adapted species as the climate warmed, how fast compared with their own spatial gradient, and is the shift specific to the temperature niche? Data: French IGN forest inventory releves (107,905 plots, 2005-2022; 15,773 plots surveyed twice) and Swedish NFI presence-absence data (38,818 visits to 14,182 permanent tracts, 1994-2024); EIVE 1.0 niche values; E-OBS temperature and rain. Method: trend of the community mean EIVE temperature value (CWM-T) with location and survey-month fixed effects; tracking fraction TF = trend / (spatial slope of CWM-T on temperature x local warming), with a bootstrap of 1-degree cells; three dose tests; a 2018-2020 extreme-summer test; a residual thermal index and species partial niche slopes that remove nitrogen, light, moisture and soil-reaction niches; observation-bias checks. Results: CWM-T increased by 0.036 (95% CI 0.027-0.049) per decade in France and 0.0078 (0.0057-0.0096) in Sweden. TF was 0.46 (0.34-0.57) and 0.32 (0.24-0.42), above the 0.12 mean of 75 earlier networks and below full tracking. The trend stayed with a fixed species pool, growing-season surveys only, richness control and within resurveyed French plots (+0.026 +- 0.006; same-month visits +0.033 +- 0.011). The residual thermal index also increased (TF 0.56 and 0.42), so the shift is not explained by eutrophication or light change. In Sweden, tracts with faster warming shifted faster (0.41 of the spatial slope, CI 0.18-0.64; 0.21 with latitude and normal controls). In France, the warming rate did not explain the geography of the shift (-0.05, CI -0.42-0.33). Short-term anomalies and the 2018-2020 hot summers gave no detectable extra shift. French change came mainly from losses of cool acidophilous species; Swedish change from gains of warmer, partly disturbance-favoured species. Limitations: expert niche values; no stand, canopy or browsing data; macroclimate only; small spatial range of warming rates; no multiplicity correction.
